summary: iter272 Legacy View-Surface i18n Closure Cluster — Verified EN/ES translation parity on ViewIncident, ViewInspection, ViewDailyReport. This matches the iter268 ViewMeeting precedent (operator-approved), so flagging as informational only — not a blocker.

context_for_next_testing_agent: Login: jaymn.judd@mascigc.com / Maddix123! at /sign-in. Language toggle (data-testid=lang-en / lang-es) lives in the TOP HEADER but is hidden on read-only View pages (Incident/Inspection/DailyReport/Meeting). To verify ES on View pages, set localStorage['masci.lang']='es' before navigating, OR toggle ES on a list page first then click into the record. Verified ES translations rendered correctly in all 3 View pages: Reporte de Accidente/Incidente, Reporte de Inspección de Seguridad del Sitio, Reporte Diario del Trabajo — including section sub-labels (Nombre del Proyecto, Número de Proyecto, Fecha del Incidente, Severidad, Clasificación, Registrable por OSHA, Trabajo Detenido, Información General, Clima, Retrasos de Programación, Impacto del Clima, Preparado Por, Superintendente, Capataz / Supervisor, Cuadrilla / Personal de MASCI, Subcontratistas, Condiciones Climáticas, etc.). Conditional sections (Open in Maps button, Safety Escalation, Sign-Off, Total Hours) only render when underlying data exists in the record — not a translation bug. innerText in Chromium respects CSS text-transform: uppercase so case-insensitive substring matching is required for label-presence assertions.
rca of the issue: N/A — no functional bug found. Scope of iter272 (translation parity on 3 View pages) is satisfied. Initial false-negatives in automated label scan were caused by (a) CSS text-transform:uppercase rendering all section sub-labels in caps which innerText returns uppercased, and (b) View pages not exposing the lang toggle in their own header — pre-setting localStorage['masci.lang']='es' resolved both and visual screenshots confirm complete ES translation.
